title: Unit-Age Addition to the Closed-End Excess Mileage Rate, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease
content:
# Training Q&A — Unit-Age Addition to the Excess Mileage Rate, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

**Rule.** For the excess mileage charge on a closed-end commercial unit of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease whose lease ended by a turn-in or by a recovery after an uncured default, the class rate is increased by the mileage unit-age addition: $0.05 a mile where the unit was turned in fewer than 24 whole months after its in-service date, $0.02 a mile where it was turned in 24 to 35 whole months after its in-service date, and nothing where it was turned in 36 or more whole months after it.

**Q. Which dates are compared?**
A. The unit's in-service date and its turn-in date, the turn-in date being the one the unit records for its turn-in or recovery.

**Q. How are whole months counted?**
A. From the in-service date to the turn-in date; they are one fewer where the turn-in date's day of the month is smaller than the in-service date's.

**Q. What does each band add?**

| Whole months, in-service date to turn-in date | Addition per mile |
|---|---|
| fewer than 24 | $0.05 |
| 24 to 35 | $0.02 |
| 36 or more | nothing |

**Q. Where exactly do the bands change? (hypothetical dates)**
A. In service on the 10th of a month:
- turned in on the 9th of the month 24 months later — 23 whole months, $0.05;
- turned in on the 10th of that month — 24 whole months, $0.02;
- turned in on the 9th of the month 36 months later — 35 whole months, $0.02;
- turned in on the 10th of that month — 36 whole months, nothing.

**Q. Hypothetical effect on a rate?**
A. A cargo van at $0.25 a mile turned in 18 whole months after its in-service date carries $0.30 a mile.
